items.title: Govern your Microsoft Fabric data estate from one place with the OneLake catalog and Govern Skills (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: The Govern experience in the OneLake catalog is now generally available, providing centralized governance capabilities for tenants, domains, capacities, workspaces, tags, and policies in Microsoft Fabric. Govern Skills are also now available in the Skills for Fabric collection, giving AI agents the knowledge they need to help admins and data owners audit, investigate, and remediate governance issues at scale. Both were announced at FabCon Europe 2026. Together, they help you monitor, manage, and act on your data estate from one place, whether you work in the Fabric portal or with an AI agent. Why it matters As AI makes it easier for more people to build with data, data estates grow in size and complexity. More workspaces, items, and access requests create more decisions about ownership, organization, and protection. Centralized, proactive governance helps admins support new projects without turning every decision into a manual review or losing visibility into how data is used. Governance can't rely on periodic, manual audits anymore. It needs to be proactive, centralized, and able to scale with the estate. items.title: Data Visualization in the Agentic Era
items.excerpt: Data visualizations help people identify patterns, trends, and outliers in their data. However, creating a useful visual requires several decisions: which chart and data to use, how to map the data to visual properties such as color and position, and how the finished visual should look. AI-assisted development can reduce that complexity by letting developers describe the intended result in natural language while reusable visualization components handle common design and interaction requirements. Deciding what visualization to create is one problem, while deciding how to create it is another. Power BI offers a convenient way to create reports and visualizations, but authors work within the chart types and formatting options that the product provides. AI coding agents another approach: developers can describe a visualization in natural language and optionally provide example images. Developers no longer have to start with a custom visual implementation or a visualization or graphics specification. Hello! items.title: Build clearer, more expressive Real-Time Dashboards with new design and KPI capabilities (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: The new, generally available authoring capabilities in Microsoft Fabric Real-Time Dashboards help authors create dashboards that are easier to scan and act on. Design Tiles add structure and context, multi-KPI groups related measures from one query, and KPI styling makes status, scale, and targets easier to interpret. Together, these capabilities give viewers a clear path from context to metrics to investigation while reducing repetitive authoring work. Figure: Camp Nou Stadium Operations Center dashboard using Design Tiles, Multi-KPI, and styled KPIs. Give your dashboard a clear structure with Design Tiles A dashboard can contain accurate visuals and still make viewers work too hard to find what matters. As service health, deployment status, business metrics, and diagnostic details accumulate, Design Tiles provide the structure, and context viewers need to identify priorities and move quickly to the right information. Design Tiles provide three focused building blocks directly on the Real-Time Dashboard canvas: Title adds a dashboard heading or a short section label. items.title: From mixed events to real-time action: Fabric Eventstreams Q3 2026
items.excerpt: Coauthor: Arindam Chatterjee Fabric Eventstreams makes it easy to connect to streaming sources, transform the ingested events and route them to destinations across Microsoft Fabric. But building real-time systems also requires teams to understand the events in motion, enriching them with business context, detecting and responding to any issues on time, and securely managing their streams across environments. That broader experience is the story behind this quarter’s updates. Eventstreams is expanding beyond connectivity and data movement to provide more of the capabilities teams need to work with streaming data after it arrives, while it is still in motion. With these expanded capabilities, users can now: Connect to more managed sources and extend Eventstreams with custom connectors. Capture change feeds from more operational databases. Explore and process multiple event types in a single Eventstream. Enrich streaming events with contextual data before processing and routing. Monitor processing health, diagnose problems, and act faster. Deploy with workspace-scoped networking and reusable configuration. items.title: Strengthening data security with workspace-level private connectivity for custom endpoints for Eventstream (Preview)
items.excerpt: Organizations that operate sensitive applications often keep them in networks with no route to the public internet. Applications in restricted networks need real-time analytics without a route to the public internet. Eventstream now supports workspace-level private links for custom endpoint sources (Preview), so those applications can send events to Microsoft Fabric over a private connection. Teams can bring sensitive operational data into real-time analytics without opening a public internet path for ingestion. The change is especially useful for in-house applications, services, and gateways that do not have a managed Eventstream connector. They can publish directly to a custom endpoint source through the workspace’s private connection, bringing these workloads into the same private networking model as supported connector-based sources. What is workspace-level private connectivity? Private Link is a network security feature of the Fabric platform that provides a private connection between a virtual network and Fabric. items.title: More ways to use scalar UDFs in Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: Scalar user-defined functions (UDFs) let data teams define a business rule once and reuse it across workloads in both Warehouse and the SQL analytics endpoint in Microsoft Fabric. This helps teams maintain consistent logic without duplicating it across queries. Some business rules require more than a single expression. They use procedural logic such as conditional branches, multiple RETURN statements, or WHILE loops. Expression Block inlining compiles and executes this logic in a distributed manner, helping reusable functions scale across analytical workloads. Building on that foundation, this update brings several improvements: More natural loop control and broader query-shape support. Automatic adoption of newly supported capabilities by existing functions, without recreating or altering them. Inlineability validation for new or changed functions, with diagnostics that explain any gaps and an explicit WITH INLINE = AUTO override when a non-inlineable function is acceptable. Express loop intent with BREAK and CONTINUE Loops often need to skip the rest of the current iteration or stop processing entirely. items.title: On-premises data gateway October 2026 release
items.excerpt: The October 2026 release of the on-premises data gateway (version 3000.338) continues our commitment to secure, reliable and accessible connectivity between on-premises data sources and Microsoft Fabric services. This release focuses on accessibility, configuration reliability, and troubleshooting. It makes the installer and configurator more inclusive, keeps your Power Query settings intact during connection tests, and makes service-start failures easier to diagnose. It also brings compatibility updates for the October 2026 release of Power BI Desktop, so queries run the same way in Power BI Desktop and in cloud refreshes. General improvements and fixes The October 2026 Gateway release (3000.338) includes Power Query Engine 2.159.229 and introduces the following improvements: Accessibility improvements in the installer and configurator Building on the accessibility work in the September release, this update improves the experience for users who rely on assistive technologies: Keyboard navigation: Moving through the gateway installer and configurator with the keyboard is smoother and more predictable. items.title: Announcing workspace monitoring integration for Fabric Data Warehouse (Preview)
items.excerpt: With Microsoft Fabric Data Warehouse integration with workspace monitoring (Preview), you can analyze completed warehouse query activity across an entire workspace from the monitoring Eventhouse and KQL database, helping you find failed or slow queries and quickly identify the warehouse that needs attention. See warehouse activity across your workspace Monitoring multiple warehouses is difficult when query activity is spread across separate tools and experiences. Workspace monitoring brings completed warehouse execution events into the WarehouseExecutions table, where administrators and operators can review activity across the workspace from a single monitoring database. The integration supports warehouses, SQL analytics endpoints, and warehouse snapshots. It captures completed, user-initiated queries that use distributed execution and records details such as duration, status, result codes, and CPU time. With this information in one place, you can spot failures or performance issues and focus your investigation on the affected warehouse and query.
